newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade $63, light - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade $63, light - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $63.00 per cwt in light volume, steady with this week's sales, feedlot sources said.
About 1,200 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area following the weekly movement of 85,700 head, according to USDA.
There were no reported sales in Kansas, with sales this week confirmed at 62,700 head, including 17,500 or about 28 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Light bids at $63.00 were being passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, the feedlot sources said.
Showlists next week were expected to be about the same number as this week, but there could be some carryover of light-weight cattle, several feedlot managers said.
The showlist this week in the Panhandle had been estimated near 81,000 head while Kansas had a showlist estimate near 78,500, market sources said.

A winter storm overnight in Kansas and Oklahoma blanketed roads with up to seven inches of snow in central Kansas, The snow made roads slippery and slowed transportation, but delays were not serious, the feedlot sources said.
